thread:
ashley: Heads up — saw a spike in exporter failures to the OTLP gRPC endpoint around 14:03 UTC. gRPC returns DEADLINE_EXCEEDED and our fallback to HTTP kicked in, which pushed CPU and blew out 99th latency. Logs show exporter.retry_reason=deadline and exporter.buffer_dropped=~10k :thinking:
samir: Ugh. Same pattern in staging earlier. Collector CPU got noisy during compaction and long RPCs piled up. We have pretty aggressive per-RPC timeouts (5s). Might be too tight for large traces/batches.
devon: Do we have a retry budget/queue configured? If retries are unbounded we could be amplifying load when backend is slow. Also fallback-to-http is heavier on CPU as you said.
eli: Quick numbers: exporter.success_rate dropped to 72% for 10m, exporter.rpc_latency_p95 spiked from 120ms -> 2.1s. HTTP fallback latency p95 ~900ms but CPU per-export increased ~30%.
ashley: Proposal: two-pronged — 1) increase RPC timeout for gRPC exports to 10s and add a conservative retry budget, 2) tighten batch sizes for exporters during backend pressure and surface a console alert for exporter.queue_dropped. Thoughts?
samir: +1 on retry budget. We should use token-bucket style budget so retries don't exceed X QPS. Also add exponential backoff with jitter. Avoid naive unlimited retries.
devon: We should also consider hedging for small/latency-sensitive traces (send 2nd request at 200ms) vs big batch traces where hedging wastes work. Maybe route by span count/size.
eli: Example otel exporter config we could try in staging: 
```
exporters:
  otlp/grpc:
    endpoint: telemetry.redwood.internal:4317
    timeout: 10s
    retry:
      enabled: true
      initial_interval: 250ms
      max_interval: 2s
      max_elapsed_time: 20s
    retry_budget:
      enabled: true
      ttl: 1m
      refill_rate: 100
      capacity: 300
batch_processor:
  scheduled_delay_millis: 200
  max_export_batch_size: 512
  max_queue_size: 10000
```
devon: That config looks reasonable. Also add gRPC channel options: keepalive pings and max_concurrent_streams so a slow collector doesn't block other streams. Eg: `grpc.max_concurrent_streams=256` and `keepalive_time_ms=60000`.
ashley: Any objections to landing a staged rollout to canary customers? We can flip on the new timeout + retry budget in staging and track exporter.success_rate, exporter.retry_cost, and console dashboard rows for dropped exports.
samir: No objections. Also add a feature flag to disable HTTP fallback temporarily so we can measure gRPC-only failure modes without the extra CPU noise.
eli: I'll add alerts: exporter.queue_dropped > 1000 in 5m, exporter.retry_cost > 10% of total exports, and exporter.rpc_deadline_exceeded rate.
infra-bot: config-change: otlp-exporter-timeout-bump rolled out to staging at 2026-03-20T15:10:00Z.
ashley: Thanks — next steps: eli adds alerts + dashboard rows, samir implements retry_budget + backoff in exporter client, devon wires gRPC channel options into runtime, i'll coordinate canary and FN flag. I'll post results here after 1h of canary traffic. :thumbsup:
